title: Staged patch backstop, synthetic-traffic rehydration, and customer pathways for canary flaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over the last quarter we have seen intermittent canary flaps that manifest as correctness regressions in hosted and private tenants, often amplified by stale KV cache state and mismatched kernel selection in private appliance builds. Several recent customer escalations required manual intervention and traffic diversion. This ticket defines a tactical "staged patch backstop" (an emergency binary and config patch path), a synthetic-traffic rehydration procedure to reconstruct prefix/KV caches in affected slices, and explicit customer-facing pathways for escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: An automated staged-patch artifact pipeline that can produce a signed emergency runtime package and an earlier compatible model variant in <= 30 minutes
A documented synthetic-traffic rehydration runbook that rebuilds KV cache prefixes and warm-starts decoders for affected tenants without impacting live traffic
Customer communication templates and SLA-based escalation handoffs documented and agreed with Support and Solutions Engineering
A test harness that validates private appliance compatibility (kernel flags, quantization profile) against the emergency package on a representative VM within 4 hours
Monitoring dashboards show KV cache warmness and post-patch quality metrics with drift thresholds and automated paging rules
implementation_steps: 1) Create a signed emergency artifact build pipeline: add 'backstop' build tag that pins conservative kernels and disables experimental kernels
2) Add an automated smoke validator that runs a quick prompt regression suite against the backstop artifact on Linux and the private appliance image
3) Implement synthetic-traffic generator scripts per-tenant that replay a compact prompt set to reconstruct prefix and KV state; these scripts must use rate limits to avoid throttle loops
4) Extend the rollout controller with a 'quarantine lane' that can route a tenant's traffic to a fenced backstop pool while preserving tokens and quotas
5) Add a rehydration orchestrator to the runtime agent that can accept a 'rehydration plan' describing prefix ranges to restore and a safe QPS envelope
6) Coordinate with Private deployment team to test the backstop package in an air-gapped environment using a signed bundle and describe manual step checklist
7) Wire up dashboards and alerts: KV cache hit-ratio, median token latency, generation quality score for sentinel prompts, and synthetic rehydration progress
8) Draft customer-facing runbooks and Support/Sales/Solutions escalation matrix and distribute to SRE and CSE teams
9) Perform a simulated incident drill with a representative enterprise tenant and document timings and gaps
rollback_strategies: Immediate traffic split: divert 90% of affected tenant traffic to last-known-good variant while keeping 10% on current to capture diagnostics
Prefix-level fence: use rollout controller to unmount problematic KV cache prefixes and fall back to remote cold fetch path (higher latency but consistent correctness)
Backstop revert: deploy the signed backstop artifact and trigger synthetic rehydration; if issues persist, pin tenant to legacy runtime image
Customer-level fast-reconnect: instruct tenant to rotate client session tokens if cache-mismatch indicates stale session-derived state
Fallback to CPU-only path for Private devices where GPU kernel mismatch is suspected (slower but avoids quantization kernel path)
monitoring_and_alerts: New metric: rehydration.progress.percent by tenant slice (alert if progress stalls > 15 minutes)
Sentinel prompt degradation score: track per-variant rolling 30-minute window (alert when delta > 10%)
KV cache divergence detector: compare prefix hashes across canary and control pools and open ticket when divergence > threshold
Synthetic traffic throttle guard: circuit-breaker that prevents rehydration from exceeding safe QPS
Pager routing: P0 pages go to SRE on-call + CSE lead + PM on-call using existing escalation channels
communications: Initial customer message template: concise summary, immediate mitigation steps taken, ETA for remediation, contact points
Daily status cadence for impacted customers until full recovery: morning summary + evening summary
Internal incident channel checklist: artifact location, rehydration plan ID, diagnostic upload link, private appliance serials
Post-incident customer debrief template and compensation guidelines linked to SLA breach analysis
